# CsExcel

> Declarative, functional Excel (.xlsx) generation for C#. Build a workbook as an immutable sequence of instructions, then render it, rather than mutating a workbook object cell by cell. A C# wrapper around FsExcel (F#), which itself builds on ClosedXML.

CsExcel is for .NET/C# developers who want a functional, declarative alternative to imperative, mutable Excel-generation APIs (such as calling ClosedXML or EPPlus directly cell-by-cell). It ships two calling styles producing identical output:

- **Vanilla** — static factory methods and collection literals, e.g. `Cell([String("x"), FontEmphasis(Bold)])`. The closest match to FsExcel's own shape.
- **Fluent** — a chainable, immutable builder, e.g. `Cell().String("x").Bold()`. Reads like a typical C# builder API; each call returns a new builder rather than mutating the one it was called on.

Install: `dotnet add package CsExcel`

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/Kookerella-Ltd/CsExcel/blob/master/README.md): overview, install, quick-start code, attribution, license
- [Vanilla API guide](https://github.com/Kookerella-Ltd/CsExcel/blob/master/Docs/Vanilla.md): static-factory calling style, walked through feature by feature
- [Fluent API guide](https://github.com/Kookerella-Ltd/CsExcel/blob/master/Docs/Fluent.md): chainable immutable-builder calling style, walked through feature by feature
- [Example project](https://github.com/Kookerella-Ltd/CsExcel/tree/master/Examples/CsExcel.Examples): runnable console app showing both styles, plus building a table from a C# record via reflection
- [FsExcel README](https://github.com/misterspeedy/FsExcel#readme): authoritative reference for the underlying declarative model CsExcel wraps
- [NuGet package](https://www.nuget.org/packages/CsExcel): published package, versions, dependencies
